body.html:
Viable Everywhere — reachable from every agent surface

Barkpark reachable from any AI surface in under two minutes, always via the mechanism that surface natively speaks — never promising a connector the surface doesn't ship. The doctrine spine is mechanism classes, not per-surface bespoke work, so the marginal cost of each new surface trends to zero. This is a dated, perishable snapshot: every mechanism below shipped Mar–Jun 2026 and vendors move monthly. All cells checked 2026-07-09; re-verified per wave.

Honesty schema (non-negotiable). Every matrix cell carries a vendor-doc citation + a check-date (2026-07-09 baseline). Soft user numbers are marked estimate/unverified — never fabricated. The tier sort key is reach × installability, never raw reach: Meta AI's 1B MAU with zero inbound path stays Tier 3.

The doctrine: mechanism classes A–D

One asset per class closes many surfaces. The paper and every slate task name surface(s) + mechanism + gate — not a per-surface project. Below, BUILT = already shipping; NET-NEW = one asset unlocks the whole class.

ClassMechanismStatus & marginal costReach it closes
A — local stdio MCPbp mcp serve + one bp onramp <target> per surfaceBUILT; near-zero per mcpServers-dialect surface~20+ coding agents
B — rules / instructions filesone canonical consumer-facing AGENTS.md emissionNET-NEW; one asset~20+ coding agents incl. the ONLY path to Aider
C — OpenAPI actionspublic /v1/openapi.json → ChatGPT Custom GPT ActionsBUILT, works todayChatGPT — the only WRITE path for Plus/Pro users
D — remote MCP (Streamable HTTP)Go NewStreamableHTTPHandler; bearer slice (low) + OAuth 2.1 AS (high)SPLIT: wave-2 bearer + wave-3 OAuth~5 chat surfaces (Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Mistral Vibe (formerly Le Chat), Grok) + Devin
Why Go-side, not Phoenix. The vendored go-sdk v1.6.1 already backing bp mcp serve ships mcp.NewStreamableHTTPHandler + auth.RequireBearerToken + the RFC 9728 PRM handler; swapping the StdioTransport line (mcp_serve.go:101) for the HTTP handler reuses the identical tool registration. The bearer verifier calls Barkpark's existing Auth.verify_token/1 choke point (auth.ex:27). CORS is a non-constraint — chat vendors call the MCP server-to-server. Citation: go-sdk v1.6.1 vendored in-repo, checked 2026-07-09.

Honesty schema (what makes a row shippable)

  • Cell = value + citation + date-checked — rows without a vendor-doc citation do not ship; the 2026-07-09 baseline stamps each matrix section.
  • Soft numbers are marked — Windsurf / Cursor / Mistral Vibe (formerly Le Chat) user bases carry (est.) or unverified; never fabricated to look precise.
  • Tier sort key = reach × installability — who can actually install matters as much as MAU. Meta AI (1B) and consumer Gemini (900M) are structurally closed and sit in Tier 3 despite their size.
  • Tier 3 rows stay present — each carries an honest one-line why-closed, not a silent omission.
  • Perishable by design — every mechanism shipped Mar–Jun 2026; the snapshot is dated and re-verified per wave, not treated as durable.

Key decisions

  1. Doctrine spine = mechanism classes A–D, not per-surface projects — one asset per class closes many surfaces.
  2. The matrix lives inside this Paper — docs/cards is at its hard cap of 7 cards, so a card is impossible; a dated, perishable snapshot belongs in a living Paper. AGENT-ONRAMPS.md gets at most a pointer row.
  3. Matrix honesty is schema — cell = value + citation + date; rows without citations don't ship; soft numbers marked estimate/unverified.
  4. Tier sort key = reach × installability — Meta AI (1B) and consumer Gemini (900M) are structurally closed → Tier 3.
  5. Roo Code is DROPPED — repo archived 2026-05-15, read-only (verified gh api repos/RooCodeInc/Roo-Code); Kilo Code (active fork) goes on the watch list.
  6. Onramp targets split into three emitter classes: (i) verbatim mcpJSONStanza reuse — Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Cline; (ii) small-new-key emitters — Copilot, Zed, Amp; (iii) new-format emitters — Continue (YAML), OpenHands (TOML).
  7. The one permitted wave-1 code slice = bp onramp windsurf + bp onramp gemini-cli — both reuse mcpJSONStanza verbatim (onramp_cmd.go:93), zero new mechanism. Cline is deferred to wave 2 (no vendor-confirmed ${env:} interpolation — an onramp must not risk writing the token into cline_mcp_settings.json).
  8. Remote MCP graduates and SPLITS, absorbing ao-backlog-remote-mcp: (a) bearer-token Streamable HTTP = Tier 1, low cost (ve-w2-remote-mcp-bearer); (b) full OAuth 2.1 AS (PKCE, /authorize + consent, /token, RFC 8707) = Tier 2 (ve-w3-oauth-as). The backlog task is patched with a supersession pointer, not duplicated.
  9. Remote MCP builds Go-side, not Phoenix — reuse the vendored go-sdk handler; REMOTE.md / onramps-charter "Phoenix-side" wording is corrected in wave 1.
  10. Class B asset = ONE plain-markdown consumer AGENTS.md emission (bp onramp agents-md) that collapses the three byte-parallel teach-layer wrappers. AGENTS.md is the ~23-tool convergence standard (agents.md, Linux Foundation).
  11. Prompt-suggestion pack is CUT — verified: no chat surface accepts an installable third-party prompt/slash pack (custom instructions / Gems / Projects are per-user config). No task filed.
  12. Skills package is Tier 2 with conservatively-cited reach — SKILL.md folder distributable on Anthropic's four surfaces (claude.ai, Claude Code, Agent SDK, API); the "20–32 adopters" list is adopter marketing, not first-party-verified.
  13. REMOTE.md is refreshed in wave 1 (doc-only): ChatGPT Plus/Pro now get read-only remote MCP via Developer Mode (2026-03-13); Claude.ai custom connectors are GA on ALL plans — the honest framing shifts from "Claude.ai can't" to "Claude.ai can, once we ship the remote endpoint."
  14. Paper publishes native blocks only via bp bulldocs publish viable-everywhere-strategy --file paper.json (body_html-only payloads fail bp paper view); linked to the epic task via the reference-edge API.
  15. llms.txt is out of scope — no provider committed, Google declined; one watch-list line, no asset.
  16. The byte-parity lock is a manual three-artifact discipline, not automation — no script reads doc bytes; the lock is a hardcoded golden constant in onramp_cmd_test.go asserted via strings.Contains, with a citation comment naming the doc file+lines. Doc stanza, printed output, and golden constant are kept identical by hand + reviewer.
  17. The full slate is FILED as published children of viable-everywhere-epic at decide time (2026-07-09) — wave-1 tasks carry full briefs; ve-w2-*/ve-w3-* are honest ledger placeholders re-briefed at their own decide phase, so the roadmap lives in the ledger, not just the charter.

body_html:
Viable Everywhere — reachable from every agent surface

Barkpark reachable from any AI surface in under two minutes, always via the mechanism that surface natively speaks — never promising a connector the surface doesn't ship. The doctrine spine is mechanism classes, not per-surface bespoke work, so the marginal cost of each new surface trends to zero. This is a dated, perishable snapshot: every mechanism below shipped Mar–Jun 2026 and vendors move monthly. All cells checked 2026-07-09; re-verified per wave.

Honesty schema (non-negotiable). Every matrix cell carries a vendor-doc citation + a check-date (2026-07-09 baseline). Soft user numbers are marked estimate/unverified — never fabricated. The tier sort key is reach × installability, never raw reach: Meta AI's 1B MAU with zero inbound path stays Tier 3.

The doctrine: mechanism classes A–D

One asset per class closes many surfaces. The paper and every slate task name surface(s) + mechanism + gate — not a per-surface project. Below, BUILT = already shipping; NET-NEW = one asset unlocks the whole class.

ClassMechanismStatus & marginal costReach it closes
A — local stdio MCPbp mcp serve + one bp onramp <target> per surfaceBUILT; near-zero per mcpServers-dialect surface~20+ coding agents
B — rules / instructions filesone canonical consumer-facing AGENTS.md emissionNET-NEW; one asset~20+ coding agents incl. the ONLY path to Aider
C — OpenAPI actionspublic /v1/openapi.json → ChatGPT Custom GPT ActionsBUILT, works todayChatGPT — the only WRITE path for Plus/Pro users
D — remote MCP (Streamable HTTP)Go NewStreamableHTTPHandler; bearer slice (low) + OAuth 2.1 AS (high)SPLIT: wave-2 bearer + wave-3 OAuth~5 chat surfaces (Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Mistral Vibe (formerly Le Chat), Grok) + Devin
Why Go-side, not Phoenix. The vendored go-sdk v1.6.1 already backing bp mcp serve ships mcp.NewStreamableHTTPHandler + auth.RequireBearerToken + the RFC 9728 PRM handler; swapping the StdioTransport line (mcp_serve.go:101) for the HTTP handler reuses the identical tool registration. The bearer verifier calls Barkpark's existing Auth.verify_token/1 choke point (auth.ex:27). CORS is a non-constraint — chat vendors call the MCP server-to-server. Citation: go-sdk v1.6.1 vendored in-repo, checked 2026-07-09.

Honesty schema (what makes a row shippable)

  • Cell = value + citation + date-checked — rows without a vendor-doc citation do not ship; the 2026-07-09 baseline stamps each matrix section.
  • Soft numbers are marked — Windsurf / Cursor / Mistral Vibe (formerly Le Chat) user bases carry (est.) or unverified; never fabricated to look precise.
  • Tier sort key = reach × installability — who can actually install matters as much as MAU. Meta AI (1B) and consumer Gemini (900M) are structurally closed and sit in Tier 3 despite their size.
  • Tier 3 rows stay present — each carries an honest one-line why-closed, not a silent omission.
  • Perishable by design — every mechanism shipped Mar–Jun 2026; the snapshot is dated and re-verified per wave, not treated as durable.

Key decisions

  1. Doctrine spine = mechanism classes A–D, not per-surface projects — one asset per class closes many surfaces.
  2. The matrix lives inside this Paper — docs/cards is at its hard cap of 7 cards, so a card is impossible; a dated, perishable snapshot belongs in a living Paper. AGENT-ONRAMPS.md gets at most a pointer row.
  3. Matrix honesty is schema — cell = value + citation + date; rows without citations don't ship; soft numbers marked estimate/unverified.
  4. Tier sort key = reach × installability — Meta AI (1B) and consumer Gemini (900M) are structurally closed → Tier 3.
  5. Roo Code is DROPPED — repo archived 2026-05-15, read-only (verified gh api repos/RooCodeInc/Roo-Code); Kilo Code (active fork) goes on the watch list.
  6. Onramp targets split into three emitter classes: (i) verbatim mcpJSONStanza reuse — Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Cline; (ii) small-new-key emitters — Copilot, Zed, Amp; (iii) new-format emitters — Continue (YAML), OpenHands (TOML).
  7. The one permitted wave-1 code slice = bp onramp windsurf + bp onramp gemini-cli — both reuse mcpJSONStanza verbatim (onramp_cmd.go:93), zero new mechanism. Cline is deferred to wave 2 (no vendor-confirmed ${env:} interpolation — an onramp must not risk writing the token into cline_mcp_settings.json).
  8. Remote MCP graduates and SPLITS, absorbing ao-backlog-remote-mcp: (a) bearer-token Streamable HTTP = Tier 1, low cost (ve-w2-remote-mcp-bearer); (b) full OAuth 2.1 AS (PKCE, /authorize + consent, /token, RFC 8707) = Tier 2 (ve-w3-oauth-as). The backlog task is patched with a supersession pointer, not duplicated.
  9. Remote MCP builds Go-side, not Phoenix — reuse the vendored go-sdk handler; REMOTE.md / onramps-charter "Phoenix-side" wording is corrected in wave 1.
  10. Class B asset = ONE plain-markdown consumer AGENTS.md emission (bp onramp agents-md) that collapses the three byte-parallel teach-layer wrappers. AGENTS.md is the ~23-tool convergence standard (agents.md, Linux Foundation).
  11. Prompt-suggestion pack is CUT — verified: no chat surface accepts an installable third-party prompt/slash pack (custom instructions / Gems / Projects are per-user config). No task filed.
  12. Skills package is Tier 2 with conservatively-cited reach — SKILL.md folder distributable on Anthropic's four surfaces (claude.ai, Claude Code, Agent SDK, API); the "20–32 adopters" list is adopter marketing, not first-party-verified.
  13. REMOTE.md is refreshed in wave 1 (doc-only): ChatGPT Plus/Pro now get read-only remote MCP via Developer Mode (2026-03-13); Claude.ai custom connectors are GA on ALL plans — the honest framing shifts from "Claude.ai can't" to "Claude.ai can, once we ship the remote endpoint."
  14. Paper publishes native blocks only via bp bulldocs publish viable-everywhere-strategy --file paper.json (body_html-only payloads fail bp paper view); linked to the epic task via the reference-edge API.
  15. llms.txt is out of scope — no provider committed, Google declined; one watch-list line, no asset.
  16. The byte-parity lock is a manual three-artifact discipline, not automation — no script reads doc bytes; the lock is a hardcoded golden constant in onramp_cmd_test.go asserted via strings.Contains, with a citation comment naming the doc file+lines. Doc stanza, printed output, and golden constant are kept identical by hand + reviewer.
  17. The full slate is FILED as published children of viable-everywhere-epic at decide time (2026-07-09) — wave-1 tasks carry full briefs; ve-w2-*/ve-w3-* are honest ledger placeholders re-briefed at their own decide phase, so the roadmap lives in the ledger, not just the charter.
